proxy_language: Proto-Quechua / Proto-Quechumaran lexical stratum of the Central Andes (Quechua I / Wanka-Jauja-Huaylas Quechua as the nearest attested descendant for Junin), with Aymara/Jaqaru as secondary comparison
proxy_rationale: Lauricocha (Huanuco) and Junin puna hunters date to roughly 10,000-6,000 BCE, millennia before any reconstructable language; their actual language is unknown and may be extinct without descendants. The defensible proxy is the highland Central Andean language stratum: Quechua I varieties (Wanka, Huaylas, Huanuco) are spoken in the same region, and the Quechumaran (Proto-Quechua / Proto-Aymara) shared lexicon covers puna ecology (camelids, tubers, cold, stone). The link to the Pleistocene/early Holocene population is weak, so names should be read as a flavour of Central Andean highland speech, not an attested hunter language. Pa, pir/pi, khu style strings in the current names are not Quechuan morphology.
phonology: Quechua I (Central) consonants: p, t, ch, k, q (uvular stop in Quechua II/southern; in Quechua I many varieties merge q into a glottal/h or lose it); aspirates and ejectives (ph th kh qh, p' t' k' q') belong to Cusco-Bolivian Quechua and Aymara, not to Central Quechua. Voiceless fricatives s, sh (in Central Quechua), h; nasals m, n, ny; liquids l, ll (palatal lateral), r; glides w, y. Three vowels /i a u/ in Proto-Quechua; Central Quechua (Wanka, Huaylas, Huanuco) additionally has long vowels (aa ii uu) giving phonemic length, and allophones [e o] near uvulars in southern varieties. Stress penultimate in most Quechua; Aymara also has penultimate stress with vowel deletion.
phonotactics: Syllable shapes (C)V(C); no onset clusters; word-initial a single consonant or vowel; codas limited to a single consonant (commonly n, r, l, y, w, s, q, k, p, t, m); medial clusters are CC across syllable boundary (e.g. -nt-, -rk-, -sq-, -ykh-). Words are overwhelmingly vowel-final because suffixes are vowel-final or CV, but roots may end in a consonant (e.g. wasi vs. kuntur). Proto-Quechua had no mid vowels e/o; spelling with e/o is conventional only near q in southern varieties.
orthography: Use the standard Quechua practical alphabet (Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua 1975 / Peruvian Ministry of Education 1985 three-vowel alphabet): a i u, ch, ll, ny, sh (Central Quechua), h, k, q, p, t, s, m, n, r, l, w, y. Long vowels written doubled (aa ii uu) in Central Quechua. Avoid Spanish-derived c, qu, gu, v, b, d, g, f, j, z, x. Ejective/aspirate marks (kh, q', t') are not used here since Central Quechua lacks them.
morphology: Agglutinative, exclusively suffixing, SOV. Roots are noun, verb or particle; nouns take number -kuna, case suffixes (genitive -pa after vowels / -pa generally, locative -pi, ablative -manta, dative/allative -man/-ta, instrumental -wan), and possessive suffixes (-y 1sg, -yki 2sg, -n 3sg, -nchik 1pl incl). Verbs take person, tense, and many derivational suffixes: -chi causative, -ku reflexive/middle, -mu directional/venitive (come/go to do), -ra- progressive/durative, -ri inceptive, -pa-/-rpa- various, -na obligation/instrument/nominal 'thing for doing', -q agentive nominalizer 'one who V's', -sqa/-shka/-sha past participle nominalizer, -y infinitive (citation form), -ypaq purposive. Diminutive -cha / -lla (restrictive 'only, just, dear'), -wan 'with', -nti 'together with'. Reduplication occurs for plural/intensive in some words (e.g., sumaq sumaq 'very beautiful').
compounding: Compounds are head-final: modifier + head (e.g., yana mayu 'black river'). 'X of Y' is Y-genitive X: Y-pa X (e.g., inti-pa wasi-n 'house of the sun', with possessor -pa and possessed -n); in compounds the genitive is often omitted: inti wasi 'sun house, temple'. Agent names use -q on a verb: rumi-ta rurakuq 'stone worker', wasi-ta ruraq; or noun + verb-q compounds like puna-pi tiyaq 'one living on the puna'. Locational names use noun + -pi/-pa-qa or place suffix -marka 'town, region' (Wanka-Jauja area: marka), -pampa 'plain, flat', -kancha 'enclosure', -wasi 'house', -mayu 'river', -qucha 'lake', -urqu 'hill/mountain', -pata 'terrace, edge'. Adjectives precede nouns and are uninflected.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier-head: adjective/possessor before head noun; demonstrative + adjective + noun; possessor in genitive (-pa) before possessed noun carrying -n (3rd person possessive).

notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word. The linguistic link between Lauricocha/Junin hunters (c. 10,000-6,000 BCE) and Quechua is speculative: the actual language is unknown, and Quechua only expanded across the Andes within the last ~2,000 years. Treat output as plausible Central Andean highland naming, avoid Spanish orthography, avoid ejectives and aspirates (not Central Quechua), use only a i u, and prefer vowel-final CV(C) syllables. The game's current strings (Piluwir pa, trukhu, muwah, Shurqur, Shunyo, Mayhu, Sapsu) include non-Quechuan features such as the sequences 'kh' before vowels with no suffix logic, final -h, and an invented particle 'pa' used as a connector; use -pa genitive plus a following possessed -n noun instead.
